content: Hi,DSGraham In most email clients and systems (such as Microsoft Outlook/Exchange or Thunderbird), retention policy enforcement does not occur immediately when the limit is reached. The timing depends on the platform used: Microsoft Outlook / Exchange (Office 365) If you use Microsoft 365 work or school email, the policy is processed by a process called the Managed Folder Assistant (MFA). Frequency: In Exchange Online, this process runs automatically every 7 days. How to speed it up: Administrators can force this process for a specific mailbox using the Start-ManagedFolderAssistant PowerShell command. Mozilla Thunderbird In Thunderbird, message limits are configured in the folder properties on the "Retention Policy" tab. Frequency: Deletion typically occurs when the folder is opened or during the folder compaction process. Note: If a folder is inactive or automatic compaction is disabled, excess messages may remain in it longer than intended.

content:
Hi,maakhenk

The problem often lies not in your phone settings, but in how folders are registered on the mail server (IMAP). Even if you see them on your laptop, they may not be subscribed for syncing with other devices. Here are the basic steps to fix this: Check folder subscriptions (IMAP) If you're using Outlook on a laptop, new folders may be created locally but not subscribed for IMAP syncing: Right-click your email account (or Inbox) in your desktop version of Outlook. Select IMAP Folders... Click the Query button to refresh the list. Find the new folders in the list, select them, and click Subscribe. Click OK and wait for syncing to complete. Mobile App Features Depending on your app, folders may simply be hidden by the interface: Outlook Mobile: Click your profile icon in the upper left corner. If there's no expand arrow next to your Inbox, try clicking the folder icon at the bottom of the menu or adding the folder to Favorites on your computer—this will ensure it appears in the mobile app. Apple Mail (iPhone): Sometimes folders don't open when you click their name. Try clicking the small blue arrow (>) to the right of the parent folder name. Gmail (Android): Make sure global sync is enabled in your account settings (Settings > Account > Use Gmail sync). Resetting an account on your phone If folders are subscribed and visible in the web interface (for example, in a browser), but not on your phone, try forcing a connection refresh: In the Outlook app on your phone, go to Settings, select your account, and click Reset Account. If that doesn't work, remove the account from your phone and re-add it. This will force the app to redownload all the folder structures from the server.
